faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Kaziranga?
faqs.answer: The park is open from November to April. February to March offers the best wildlife sighting opportunities as the grasslands are shorter.

faqs.question: Will I definitely see a rhinoceros?
faqs.answer: Kaziranga has the highest density of one-horned rhinos in the world. While wildlife sightings can never be guaranteed, the success rate is extremely high — over 95% of visitors spot at least one rhino.

faqs.question: Is the jeep safari safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, all safaris are conducted with experienced forest guides and follow strict park safety protocols. Vehicles maintain safe distances from animals at all times.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Living Root Bridge trek?
faqs.answer: The trek involves approximately 3,500 steps each way. It's of moderate difficulty — a reasonable level of fitness is recommended. We provide an experienced local guide and suggest starting early to avoid the midday heat.

faqs.question: Does it rain a lot in Meghalaya?
faqs.answer: Cherrapunji is one of the wettest places on Earth, but October to May is relatively dry and the best time to visit. Light rain is always possible — we recommend packing a rain jacket.

faqs.question: Is the Dawki River really that clear?
faqs.answer: Yes! The Umngot River at Dawki is famous for its crystal-clear turquoise water, especially from November to March. Boats appear to float on air — it's a surreal experience.

faqs.question: Do I need a special permit for Arunachal Pradesh?
faqs.answer: Yes, Indian citizens need an Inner Line Permit (ILP). We handle the complete permit process for you — just share your ID proof and photos before the trip.

faqs.question: Is altitude sickness a concern?
faqs.answer: Sela Pass reaches 13,700 ft. Most travelers handle it fine with gradual acclimatization (our itinerary is designed for this). We recommend staying hydrated and avoiding heavy exertion at altitude.

faqs.question: Can Bum La Pass visit be guaranteed?
faqs.answer: Bum La Pass requires special Indian Army permission that is granted on a day-to-day basis. We apply for it, but it depends on weather and security conditions. If denied, we substitute with alternative sightseeing.

faqs.question: How fit do I need to be for this tour?
faqs.answer: The Nongriat trek (Day 4) is moderately challenging with ~3,500 steps. Other days involve light walking. A basic fitness level is sufficient for most activities.

faqs.question: Can activities like cliff jumping be skipped?
faqs.answer: Absolutely! All adventure activities are optional. You can enjoy the scenery and swimming without any extreme activities.

faqs.question: Is the snorkeling in Dawki safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, the river is calm and shallow in the snorkeling areas. Equipment and guidance are provided. It's available October to March when water clarity is at its best.

faqs.question: Is the road to Tawang safe?
faqs.answer: The roads are mountain roads maintained by BRO (Border Roads Organisation). Our experienced drivers are familiar with every turn. We use 4x4 vehicles for maximum safety.

faqs.question: What's the weather like in Tawang?
faqs.answer: Tawang is cold year-round. Even in summer, temperatures range 5-20°C. In winter, it can drop below freezing. Pack heavy woolens regardless of season.

faqs.question: What makes this the 'ultimate' Arunachal tour?
faqs.answer: This is our most comprehensive Arunachal package — it includes both Bum La Pass (India-China border) and Madhuri Lake, which are not included in the shorter 5D or 6D packages. It also allows a full day in Tawang for unhurried exploration.

faqs.question: Is this trip suitable for senior citizens?
faqs.answer: The trip involves long drives and high altitudes. Seniors in good health can enjoy it, but we recommend consulting a doctor about altitude sickness precautions. The itinerary doesn't involve any mandatory trekking.

faqs.question: What happens if weather blocks Sela Pass?
faqs.answer: In rare cases of heavy snowfall, Sela Pass may be temporarily closed. We monitor conditions closely and adjust the itinerary if needed — usually a delay of a few hours. Full blockages are very rare during the recommended travel season.
